chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Durays al-Kunasi who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying — while in his presence were people from his companions — 'I am astonished at a group of people who show loyalty to us and make us their Imams, and describe that obedience to us is obligatory upon them just as obedience to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), yet then they break their own argument and defeat themselves by the weakness of their hearts, so they diminish our right and blame that upon those whom God has given the proof of the right knowledge of us and submission to our command.'

Do you think that God, Blessed and Exalted, would make obedience to His guardians obligatory upon His servants, and then hide from them the news of the heavens and the earth, and cut off from them the sources of knowledge regarding what comes to them of that by which their religion is upheld?

So Humran said to him: 'May I be your ransom! What is your view of what occurred regarding the rising of Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them) — their going forth and their rising with the religion of God, Mighty is His mention — and what befell them from the tyrants killing them and being victorious over them until they were killed and overcome?'

So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Humran! Indeed God, Blessed and Exalted, had already decreed that upon them, and ordained it, and carried it through, and made it inevitable — on the path of their free choice — then He brought it about. It was by the preceding knowledge conveyed to them from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) that Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them) rose, and it was by knowledge that those of us who remain silent, remained silent.'

And had they, O Humran, when there descended upon them what descended from the command of God, Mighty and Majestic, and the victory of the tyrants over them — had they asked God, Mighty and Majestic, to repel that from them, and had they persisted in seeking the removal of the tyrants' kingdom and the end of their rule, He would have answered them and repelled that from them, and the expiry of the tyrants' period and the annihilation of their kingdom would have come faster than the dispersal of beads when their thread is cut and they scatter.

And that which befell them, O Humran, was not due to a sin they had committed nor due to punishment for disobedience by which they opposed God; rather, it was for the ranks and honor from God that He wanted them to attain. So do not let false opinions lead you astray regarding them.

key_terms.أولياء: Guardians/saints — here referring to the Imams as divinely appointed guardians
key_terms.الاختيار: Free choice — emphasizing that the Imams' risings were chosen, not merely fated
key_terms.حجة: Proof/argument — the doctrinal proof of the Imam's authority
key_terms.طاعة: Obedience — obligatory compliance with the commands of the Imams, equivalent in status to obedience to the Prophet
key_terms.طواغيت: Tyrants — those who transgressed and rose against the Imams
key_terms.قوام الدين: Uprightness/support of religion — what sustains religious practice
key_terms.منازل وكرامة: Stations and honor — the elevated divine ranks attained through martyrdom
key_terms.مواد العلم: Sources/mines of knowledge — referring to the divine knowledge granted to the Imams

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn suffer defeat if the Imams possess divine knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through Durays al-Kunasi from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), addresses two profound theological questions: (1) the inconsistency of those who profess belief in the Imams' authority yet deny their divine knowledge, and (2) the question of why the early Imams—Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn—suffered defeat and martyrdom if they possessed divine knowledge and authority. The Imam explains that the sufferings of Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn were divinely decreed, chosen willingly by them through their foreknowledge from the Prophet, and were not punishments but elevations to the highest stations of honor. The historical context is the early Abbasid period when discussions about the nature of Imamate and the tragedy of Karbala were urgent theological debates in Shia communities.

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying, and in his<sup>asws</sup> presence were people from his<sup>asws</sup> companions: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> am astounded from a group of people who are befriending us<sup>asws</sup> and making us<sup>asws</sup> to be their Imams<sup>asws</sup>, and are describing that obedience to us<sup>asws</sup> is a necessity upon them just like the obedience to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, then they are breaking their own arguments and are debating against themselves due to their weak hearts, so they are being deficient in our<sup>asws</sup> rights, and they are (then) faulting that upon the ones whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Granted the substantiation of the right of our<sup>asws</sup> recognition, and the submission to our<sup>asws</sup> orders.

Are you viewing that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High would Necessitate the obedience to His<sup>azwj</sup> Guardians<sup>asws</sup> upon His<sup>azwj</sup> servants, then He<sup>azwj</sup> would Hide the news of the skies and the earth and cut-off the Mine of the Knowledge from them<sup>asws</sup>, regarding what is referred to them<sup>asws</sup> from what wherein is the straightness of their Religion?’

So Humran said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What is your<sup>asws</sup> view of what was from the matter of the risings of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>, and Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, and their<sup>asws</sup> coming out and their<sup>asws</sup> rising with the Religion of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Mighty is His<sup>azwj</sup> Mention, and what hit them<sup>asws</sup> from the tyrants murdering them<sup>asws</sup> and being victorious with them<sup>asws</sup> until they murdered and overcame?’

So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Humran! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High had already Determined that upon them<sup>asws</sup>, and Ordained it, and Accomplished it, and Made it to be inevitable upon the way of the choice (by them<sup>asws</sup>). Then He<sup>azwj</sup> Caused it to flow. Thus, it was by the preceding of knowledge to them<sup>asws</sup> from Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> that Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> arose, but (on the other hand) it was due to (that) knowledge remains silent, the one<sup>asws</sup> from us<sup>asws</sup> who is silent.

And had they<sup>asws</sup>, O Humran, when it descended with them what descended from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and the victories of the tyrants upon them<sup>asws</sup>, asked Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic that He<sup>azwj</sup> Defends them<sup>asws</sup> from that, and insisted upon it with regards to the decline of the kingdoms of the tyrants and the annihilation of their kingdoms, then He<sup>azwj</sup> would have Answered them<sup>asws</sup> and Defended them<sup>asws</sup> from that, then it would have been so that the expiry of the duration of the tyrants and the annihilation of their kingdoms would have been quicker than the dispersal of the beads when their string is cut off, so it would have dispersed.

And it was not so, that, that which hit them<sup>asws</sup>, O Humran, was neither due to sins they<sup>asws</sup> had committed nor was it a Punishment due to disobedience opposing Allah<sup>azwj</sup> therein, but it was due to the status and Benevolence from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Intending that they<sup>asws</sup> reach it. Therefore, do not let the (false) principles take you to be among them’ (who oppose the truth).
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Durays al-Kunasi who has said that he heard abu Ja‘far (a.s.) the following to an audience of his companions.

“What an strange case is the case with a group of followers! They acknowledge us as the Divine authority over themselves, accept us as their Imam and say that obedience to us is obligatory just as is the case with the Messenger of Allah. They then destroy the veracity of their belief as such and dispute against their own selves due to weakness of their hearts. They then diminish our right and blame those whom Allah has granted evidence to know us as it should be and the (abulity) to submit themselves to our Divine authority. Do you not consider that how would Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, make it obligatory to obey those who possess Divine authority over his servants and then hide from them (people who possess Divine authority) `the new of the heaves and the earth? How would He cut them off of the sources of knowledge that might come to them to maintain their religion?”

Humran then said to the Imam (a.s.), “May Allah, take my soul in service for your cause, how would you explain the case of the uprising of Ali ibn abu Talib, al-Hassan and al-Husayn (a.s.)? They came out and rose up for the cause of Allah, Whose mention is so Majestic. How much they suffered and how mercilessly were they murdered at the hands of the rebels? They were defeated, murdered and over powered.”

Abu Ja‘far (a.s.) then said, “O Humran, Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, had determined it on them. He had decreed, approved and made it unavoidable though the voluntary manner. He then allowed to take place. It, thus, happened with a pre-existing knowledge that had come to them from the Messenger of Allah. Ali al-Hassan and al-Husayn (a.s.) rose up for the cause of Allah with full knowledge of the consequences and remained silent from us those who remained silent.

Had they, O Humran, when facing what Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, made them to face and suffer defeat at the hands of the rebels, asked Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, to remove their suffering and would implore Him to destroy the government and kingdom of the rebels He would have answered their prayers and would grant them relief. In such case the destruction of the governments of the rebels and the ending of their time would take place quicker than the dispersal under a great pressure, of beads threaded together.
The suffering, O Humran, that befell them, because of the sins that they might have committed or the punishment for their opposition to Allah.
It was because of the high marvelous position that Allah had prepared and wanted them to reaCh Do not let people’s opinions take you away from the right path.”
